messages.subject: Questions about Matrix C
parts:
Hi, Dr. Jiang,

Thanks for your contribution with such a great software tool Canopy.

After reading all illustrations about matrix C, I still can't understand it. 

For example, in MDA231 sample data, I guess chr7_1 and chr7_2 overlapped with each other. however, there are no more information about chr7_1 and chr7_2.
I can't find any numbers related to these two symbols from matrix X, Y, WM, Wm,R.

Could you kindly explain it more detailedly?  

Thanks

Chuan Jiang

messages.author: 94ec915e8ce36448
messages.subject: Re: [canopy_phylogeny] Questions about Matrix C
parts:
Hi Chuan,

Thanks for your interest in Canopy and sorry for my late reply — I just got back from travel. Here is a more detailed explanation on how to generate the C matrix: https://github.com/yuchaojiang/Canopy/blob/master/instruction/overlapping_CNA.md .

Specifically, for this dataset, we know chr7 has two CNA events (supplementary Figure S13) with different breakpoints. However for this CNA region in Figure S13, we only have one CNA input for a specific sample, i.e., we won’t know the chr7_1 and chr7_2 input for each sample until we perform the deconvolution.

I am working on more detailed illustration on overlapping CNAs and I hope to push the update onto GitHub soon. Also please update your package via GitHub — I made significant changes last week.

Feel free to let me know if you have further questions.

Best,
Yuchao

messages.author: 94ec915e8ce36448
messages.subject: Re: [canopy_phylogeny] Questions about Matrix C
parts:
Yes that is theoratically correct. Although whole genome doubling event can be hard to detect and in this case it can be even harder to let the algorithm deconvolute itself. You can definitely try this though and see if the results make sense.

One way to make this easier if you are sure that the doubling event is true is to fix a genome-wide doubling event at the first split of the tree so that all subsequent events happen after this. This is not enabled by Canopy though you might have to zoom into the source code and modify a bit.

Yuchao
